I don't have any notes for you yet. My research tool stopped me before I could read a single page, so I have nothing from the approved sites to report.

I sent requests for six pages, but my code crashed before it showed me what came back. When I tried to look at the results, the tool said I'd hit the limit on tool calls for this turn. My other tools can't reach the internet, so I had no other way to search or read pages. Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything.

These are the pages I tried to read:
- Enduring Word: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jonah-3/
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/jonah/3.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/jonah/3.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/jonah/3.htm
- Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/jonah-3-commentary
- NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Jonah+3

If you ask again, I'll start by reading those six pages properly. Then I'll search the other sites on your list for the points most likely to show real differences:
- **v. 3:** what "three-day journey" means.
- **v. 5:** whether the Ninevites truly turned to God.
- **vv. 7–8:** why the animals take part in the fast.
- **vv. 9–10:** in what sense God "relented", and how that fits with God not changing. This is where Reformed, Wesleyan, Catholic and Orthodox writers are most likely to differ.
- **Background:** modern scholars' views on whether the events happened as told.
